biography.plain_text: Edoardo Longarini was an Italian construction entrepreneur from Tolentino and the founder of Adriatica Costruzioni. Public reconstruction concessions in Ancona, Macerata and Ariano Irpino underpinned his business. He also became a regional newspaper publisher, building a network of Gazzette titles across the Marche, Umbria and Tuscany alongside his construction interests.

long_biography.plain_text:
Italian businessman Edoardo Longarini financed Ancona Calcio's rise to Serie A and its appearance in a Coppa Italia final. He entrusted the club's formal presidency to Camillo Florini, while retaining approval over important decisions. Coach Vincenzo Guerini worked with that arrangement during the team's most successful period.

At Ternana, Longarini provided financial backing while his sons Emanuele and Simone took leadership roles. During his ownership, the club developed a youth link with Rome's Borghesiana Soccer Academy, recruiting a team from the surrounding area. The family eventually transferred Ternana to Unicusano, ending more than a decade of ownership.

uncertainties.detail: All current-relationship language refers to Longarini's terminal lifetime, ending 1 September 2020. Adriatica was in liquidation and its economic relationships were personally assigned to him. The positive continuity of construction-derived assets supports medium-confidence terminal industry and founder relationship. No complete estate valuation establishes net wealth or an exact sector share. Nominal arbitration awards, claims and government payment amounts are not treated as retained net assets; liabilities and subsequent reversals can matter.

Broad Self-made rests on a documented founder-built substantial business and his economic ownership, not absence of inheritance. The reported railway-worker father does not settle initial funding or access. Political connections described by reporting do not alone establish inherited family privilege or a launch platform; no independent-start subtype is inferred.

Edoardo was the financial owner/patron; sons Emanuele and Simone held club leadership roles. Ternana passed to Unicusano before his death. Later family estate activity is not attributed to him. The youth report supports Ternana's recruitment initiative, not the stronger secondary claim that Edoardo personally founded Borghesiana Soccer Academy.

Forbes-first and follow-up searches produced no matching profile. Personal LinkedIn, Instagram, website, Twitter, Facebook, YouTube and TikTok searches found no verified account. LinkedIn directory names alone were insufficient; the official scientist profile is a clear namesake rejection. Football-club social accounts are institutional, not personal. No company site securely representing his terminal owned platform was established; Wikipedia alone is proposed. No relevant Trip Advisor, Zillow, Vimeo or Flickr profile established.

Some profiles date Adriatica's founding to the 1970s, while parliamentary records identify concessions to the company in 1964. No founding year is published here. A sports profile gives Ancona/1932 and architecture education; official Tolentino/1931 controls birth details, and unsupported education is omitted.

The source snapshot lists death fields as inapplicable because the old record said Alive; it is preserved exactly. The supported mortality correction is proposed. Proven 1 September 2020 death fields are high-confidence review candidates pending a refreshed post-correction input, since current validation rejects those blank-field proposals. The regional ANSA mirror did not open; original ANSA was accessible. Court copies were readable. Legal and health details not needed for biography are omitted.

Heavy civil construction, Newspaper publishing and Football satisfy active semantic contracts. Generic Publishing duplicates the narrower tag; separate club ownership does not establish a wealth-creating multi-club model. No tag created for unrepresented companies, no weak shipbuilding tag inferred from personal yacht ownership, and no formal taxonomy candidate.
